title: Sparse qubit operation in a 6$\times$6 quantum dot array
authors: Alexader S. Ivlev, Harold L. Co, Damien R. Crielaard, Alice Petrillo, Setareh Kazemzadeh, Giordano Scappucci, Menno Veldhorst
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires increasing the qubit count while maintaining high performance and connectivity. Semiconductor qubits have demonstrated high-fidelity operation, but growing the system size at sufficient connectivity remains challenging, such that scaling mainly occurred in one spatial direction to preserve access for control lines in the other. Here, we realise an approach that relaxes the requirements on fabrication and demonstrate a 6$\times$6 quantum dot array, defined by a shared barrier gate and individual plunger gates. The quantum dots are tuned through coherent spin shuttling over distances up to 5.2um into a sparse configuration of 10 simultaneously operated qubits, leaving space for shuttling connections. We reduce crosstalk by 42$\times$ in this separated regime, enabling high-fidelity simultaneous single-qubit control, while control-Z operations can be implemented through shuttling and plunger-only control. These results promise high-connectivity quantum circuits, enabled by scaling to two-dimensional geometries and exploiting shuttling.
summary: This paper reports on the realization and characterization of a large, $6 	imes 6$ quantum dot array for quantum computation. By employing coherent spin shuttling, the researchers overcome connectivity limitations, achieving high-fidelity single-qubit control and two-qubit gates between distant qubits. The work demonstrates a promising path toward scalable, solid-state quantum processors.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving scalable, high-connectivity quantum computation using semiconductor spin qubits while overcoming physical limitations like wiring bottlenecks and poor 2D connectivity.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a $6 	imes 6$ quantum dot array capable of high-fidelity single-qubit control and two-qubit gates via coherent spin shuttling, significantly reducing crosstalk in the process.
method: The research employs coherent spin shuttling techniques to position qubits sparsely within a large array, enabling high-fidelity gate operations and state transfer between distant sites.
model_or_system: The platform is a $6 	imes 6$ quantum dot array realized in a semiconductor heterostructure, controlled by shared barrier and individual plunger gates. Qubit operations rely on manipulating electron/hole spins via electric fields and controlled exchange interactions.
key_observables: Single-qubit Clifford fidelities ($>99\%$), round-trip transfer fidelity ($99.4\%$), crosstalk reduction ($42	imes$), and two-qubit CZ gate fidelities ($\sim 88.6\%$).
important_parameters: Shuttling distances up to $5.2 \mu	ext{m}$; exchange interaction ($J$) tunable over orders of magnitude; gate times and detunings are critical parameters.
main_assumptions: The fidelity is highly sensitive to imperfections in the necessary 'recovery gates' used to compensate for shuttling-induced rotations, which is a major source of error.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $6 	imes 6$ array structure, SED measurements for charge mapping, time-resolved spin paths, and characterization plots for single-qubit and two-qubit gate fidelities.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from demonstrating basic state preparation and single-qubit control via shuttling, to implementing two-qubit gates (CZ) by bringing qubits into proximity, and finally detailing the complex calibration of the shuttling process itself.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, scalable solid-state platform for quantum computation, directly addressing the engineering challenge of scaling connectivity beyond simple linear chains, which is a major focus in quantum information theory.
